integrationIssue: #617. The family is deliberately UNREGISTERED at HEAD: catalogue registration, blueprint regeneration and CLI wiring all ride the #617 regeneration wave under owner ruling R5 (#510). That issue owns the four cells this artifact records OPEN.
note: The per-family closure surface for Q39 (`fabricated-deposit`) at GOAL_SPEC.md 9.1. It publishes the outputs 1 to 10 status list for this one family with the exact evidence behind each output, and it derives every status from a measurement rather than asserting it, so a cell closes when the tree changes and not when this prose changes. Every count here was produced by demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-proof-family-q39.mjs in this tree: one batched `aiken check -e` invocation under the pinned fork compiler for the 16 on-chain selectors, one Vitest run per cited suite, and one run-time adversarial proof-fit sweep that builds a real 10000-leaf deposits MPF and encodes this family's real step redeemers and datums through the SDK's own codec. Nothing is counted from test source, from prose, or from a sibling artifact's numbers. LOCAL_PASS is the only passing status this artifact may record; the live half of a family's closure is owned exclusively by the Q57 sweep and QG3 and is never recorded in a family-local artifact. Four things differ structurally from the Q10/Q11/Q12/Q14 twins. First, nothing is delegated: this family is not one of the four in the shared Q1x artifact, so output 5's adversarial proof-fit is measured HERE, family-locally, at run time. Second, this family opens NONE of the nine section-2.5 committed fields, so output 3 is measured as an ABSENCE plus the anchoring that does bind — the counted deposits_root under DepositsRootDomain and the two 32-byte content commitments — the shape the Q12 twin uses. Third, four cells are OPEN rather than LOCAL_PASS because the surfaces they name do not exist at HEAD by design: the family is absent from the append-only catalogue order, its eight blueprint titles are absent from the frozen blueprint, `bin.ts` carries no verb for it, and neither coverage matrix records it. Each of those four statuses is DERIVED from the measurement, so the #617 wave closes them without an edit to this prose. Fourth, output 9's emulator suite is measured through a purpose-built derivation rather than the shared one: the suite deliberately stops at the frozen-blueprint boundary with a runtime skip, which the shared `deriveVitestOutcome` rejects outright, so the gate measures exactly one collected test with status `skipped`, zero failures, exit 0, and the eight-title absence the block itself asserts.

compiler.rationale: .github/workflows/aiken-ci.yml runs exactly one compiler. The stock v1.1.22 build that used to hold the compilation role ships a live unsound-codegen defect and is retired from every role, so it is not a second authority to agree with. The identity is measured from the spawned binary and required to match this pin EXACTLY rather than by prefix: a second fork build of the same 1.1.23 base reports a different `+<rev>` suffix and would supply this family's on-chain result under a compiler the workflow does not pin.

output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.rule: A block header may not commit a deposit leaf whose identity never existed on L1, or whose content misstates the authentic L1 deposit event that was due for that block. Concretely: for a committed `(DepositId, DepositInfo)` leaf of the challenged header's counted `deposits_root`, either no deposit event with that `DepositId` was ever authenticated on L1 — witnessed by the output at that very reference still being unspent, because `midgard/user_events`'s `authenticate_new_event` can only mint an event NFT by spending it — or such an event exists and its `DepositInfo` commitment differs from the committed one, with the event's inclusion time inside the challenged header's window `start_time < inclusion_time <= end_time`.

catalogueBinding.derivation: The deployed identifier is the positional index of the category in the append-only order, encoded big-endian over FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_ID_BYTE_COUNT bytes. `fabricatedDeposit` is measured ABSENT from the order, whose length is measured at 11, so index 11 is the next append slot and `0000000b` is the id the family reserves. Both the on-chain constant and the SDK constant are required to equal that derived value, so the reservation cannot drift from the order it is derived from: if #617 registers this family by INSERTING rather than appending, the order length changes, the derived id changes, and this cell fails closed instead of silently renumbering every family after it.

onchainDecisionSites.role: admission: the computation thread's token must be filed under this family's category id, so a thread minted under another family's category cannot be run here
conviction: the classified fault must be established, and on the content arm the authentic event's inclusion time must fall inside the challenged header's window

measuredRuleEnforcementTitles: refuses an absence claim that rests on a consumed UTxO, and any witness that is not authenticated L1 security-grade evidence
refuses a present-event witness that is not bound to the committed identity
refuses to challenge a header that committed exactly the authentic content
refuses an authentic event that was not due for the challenged block, on either side of the window
output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.ruleEnforcementNote: These four titles are the rule's own conditions, exercised off-chain: the absence arm's live-output requirement, the present-event arm's binding to the committed identity, the valid-block guard when the header committed exactly the authentic content, and the inclusion window on both of its sides. They are required to have EXECUTED and PASSED in the runner report rather than to exist in source.
output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.whyNoLocalRejectCode: This rule is not an L2 transaction-validation rule, so it has no `RejectCodes` member and no phase-A/phase-B enforcement site to count. It is a BLOCK-level fabrication: the fault is in what a header committed about L1, not in a transaction the block contained. The measured enforcement is therefore on-chain, in the two named decision sites, and the off-chain side contributes the violation identifier and the reserved category id rather than a local rejection.

enums.label: the opening of step-02's retained commitment

output2SchemaAndCodecAgreement.whyPositional: Every one of these four enums crosses the boundary as a Plutus constructor index, so constructor ORDER is wire format. A set comparison of arm names would accept a swap of Constr 0 and Constr 1 — which on the verdict enum would turn an authenticated absence into an authenticated observation — so each enum's arms are compared as an ordered list on both sides.

The alias is what makes that shared schema THIS family's schema; if it were ever rewritten into a family-local re-declaration, the parity this cell publishes would stop binding here.

absenceSweep.why: The absence is MEASURED across all eight family-owned Aiken modules, over comment-stripped source, rather than inferred from the family's description. No section-8.8 door symbol, no field index and no field hash appears anywhere in this family: it never opens a committed transaction field, because the fault it proves is about the block's deposit source set rather than about a transaction the block contained.

countedRootCall.why: This is where the family gets its positional identity, in place of a committed-field index. The counted-root wrapper hashes the cardinality into the root, so the witness cannot keep the raw MPF root and quietly restate a different `deposit_count`; and the very bytes fed to the counted-root check are the bytes the 32-byte content commitment is taken over, so the leaf the family adjudicates is exactly the leaf the header committed.

contentCommitments.label: step-02's retained commitment to the authentic event datum

openedPreimageSite.pairingRefusal: fail @"fabricated-deposit: opening does not pair with the L1 verdict"
openedPreimageSite.why: The one preimage this family opens is not a committed transaction field: it is step-02's retained commitment to the AUTHENTIC L1 event datum. The opening is checked against that commitment, and it is required to pair with the verdict it inherited, so a prover who found the authentic event cannot switch to the empty opening and convert a content dispute into the strictly stronger non-existence claim.

output3CommittedFieldBinding.whyLocalPass: Output 3 is an ABSENCE plus an anchoring, the shape the Q12 twin publishes. The absence is measured across all eight modules rather than asserted, so a future edit that reaches for the section-8.8 door fails this cell instead of quietly widening the family's surface; and the anchoring that DOES bind the adjudicated bytes — the counted `deposits_root`/`deposit_count` pair under `DepositsRootDomain`, plus the two 32-byte content commitments and the single checked preimage opening — is measured in the modules that perform it.

selectors.claim: the challenged header's counted deposits_root really commits the disputed (DepositId, DepositInfo) leaf, so step-01 forwards the committed identity, a 32-byte commitment to the committed content, and the header's inclusion window

fabricating a deposit against a valid block means exhibiting a deposits MPF that is not the one the header committed — a tree over a different DepositId carried with its own counted root — and the counted-root equality against header.deposits_root refuses it

the witness's restated count must be the header's deposit_count: the count is hashed into deposits_root, so a witness cannot keep the raw MPF root and quietly change the cardinality the block committed to

a thread minted under another family's catalogue category cannot be run here, because its fraud-proof token would be filed under that other category's rule; the substituted prefix is transition_trace's own 00000004

both admissible L1 witnesses authenticate: the still-unspent output at the committed DepositId yields DepositIdentityAbsent, and the authentic event UTxO under the hub-registered deposit policy yields DepositEventObserved with a commitment to the exact event datum bytes and the event's inclusion time

the event NFT must be minted under the policy the hub oracle registers: anyone can mint a token with the right asset name under their own policy, so without this the authentic event would be whatever the prover minted

the absence witness must be the live output at exactly the committed DepositId; on a valid block that output is spent — the spend is what authenticated the event — so a prover attacking a valid block can only offer some other still-unspent output, and this is where that substitution is refused
a reference input carrying a well-formed DepositDatum but no event NFT at all is not evidence, because any user can build that output, so untrusted material must never reach the verdict

both faults are classified from authenticated material: the content-mismatch arm re-opens the exact event datum step-02 committed to and shows its DepositInfo commitment differs from the one the header committed, and the nonexistent-identity arm carries the absence verdict forward with nothing left to open

a header that commits exactly the authentic event's DepositInfo has fabricated nothing and no fault can be classified from it: the committed commitment and the authentic one are equal, so there is no mismatch to name

the opened preimage must be the bytes step-02 authenticated: a one-integer edit to the inclusion time is enough to change the commitment and the hash equality refuses it, so the authentic content cannot be whatever the prover chose to supply

the opening must pair with the verdict it inherited: a prover who found the authentic event may not switch to the NoAuthenticContent opening, which would convert a content dispute into a strictly stronger non-existence conviction and let a real deposit be erased rather than corrected

both faults finalize into a permanent fraud-proof token under this family's category: the content-mismatch arm carries two different content commitments and an event that was due for the challenged block, and the nonexistent-identity arm carries the absence verdict step-02 authenticated

a block that committed exactly the authentic deposit is not convictable: even if such a thread reached the final step, the mismatch it carries names the same content commitment twice and no permanent token is minted for it

the authentic event must have been due for the challenged block under start_time < inclusion_time <= end_time; an event that became due after the block ended is the inclusion-window family's rule, and convicting on it here would let one fault be proven twice under two categories

the fault must be filed against the header the thread token names, because the minted fraud-proof token inherits that asset name, so a thread whose state names a different block would publish its conviction against the wrong header

output4OnchainSelectors.roleDerivation: Roles are read from the DECLARATION FORM, not from names: a selector is a negative if and only if its declaration is `test <name>() fail`, and the measured `on_failure` field of the compiler's own report is required to agree — `succeed_eventually` for every negative and `fail_immediately` for every positive. That is two independent sources for the same role, so a `fail` keyword deleted from source while the name still starts with `rejects_` fails this cell.
output4OnchainSelectors.scopeDerivation: Every selector's scope is derived by resolving whether its body reaches its own module's `main.spend`, directly or through the transitive closure of module-local helpers that do. All 16 resolve to the handler, and the published route is the resolved helper chain per selector, so a selector that stops testing a helper instead of the validator cannot be counted as step-scoped.
output4OnchainSelectors.perStepRequirement: Output 4's requirement is checked PER STEP MODULE on the step-scoped selectors: each of the four modules is required to have at least one step-scoped positive and at least one valid-block negative. All four do, exactly one of each.

formatGate.why: The eight family-owned modules are required to be byte-identical to what the pinned fork's own `aiken fmt` produces. It matters here beyond tidiness: this gate parses those modules for roles, scopes, handler reach and token absence, and a reformat that moved a `test ... fail` declaration off the start of a line would change what the parses measure. The format script resolves the fork by MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN / MIDGARD_FORK_AIKEN_BIN and refuses to guess a formatter, so it cannot normalize under the retired build.

output5AdversarialProofFit.whyNotDelegated: This family is not one of the four bound by the shared docs/exec-plans/evidence/canonical-v1-proof-family-q1x-v1.json artifact, so no sibling gate measures its proof fit. The sweep runs family-locally, at gate run time, in demo/scripts/verify-canonical-v1-proof-family-q39.mjs, and adds no test file.
output5AdversarialProofFit.l1ByteLimitSource: PROTOCOL_PARAMETERS_DEFAULT.maxTxSize, read at run time out of the @lucid-evolution/lucid build the family's own package resolves
output5AdversarialProofFit.rule: l1ByteMargin >= 0 for every step of the family, at the worst supported committed-deposit cardinality and the largest membership proof that cardinality admits

cardinalityBound.why: The adversarial axis for this family is the depth of the committed deposits MPF membership path, and the header's own `deposit_count` bound is what caps it. The bound is read out of the Aiken source at run time rather than restated, so a change to the normative cardinality re-runs the whole sweep against the new number.

codecAnchoring.why: The sweep measures bytes through the SDK's own codec, which is a built artifact and therefore not itself tracked. So the codec is anchored before it is trusted: the two Aiken-measured leaf constants are read out of the tracked family suite, decoded through the SDK schemas, re-encoded through `committedDepositKeyBytesV1` / `committedDepositValueBytesV1`, and required to reproduce the exact same bytes. A stale or divergent build fails the sweep at its first step instead of publishing sizes taken under a codec nobody checked.

output5AdversarialProofFit.ladderSelection: At every rung the sweep builds a real deposits MPF over that many canonical `(DepositId, DepositInfo)` leaves and proves EVERY leaf, then keeps the proof with the most CBOR bytes — not the proof with the most steps. Those are different leaves: at 10000 leaves the byte-maximising proof is 770 bytes while a step-maximising one measures 704, because a step's kind decides its size. Selecting on steps would have published a 66-byte-optimistic worst case.

closedForm.why: Every rung of the measured ladder is reproduced exactly by this closed form, which is what licenses extrapolating the byte envelope past the cardinality the sweep can build. The 139-byte branch step is measured here independently and agrees with the number the shared Q1x artifact pins for the same machinery.

worstCase.fixedWidthPlaceholderNote: Every field of the thread states and of the non-membership redeemer arms is a fixed-width hash or key hash, so the sweep fills them with placeholders of the declared widths and the measured byte counts do not depend on the placeholder values. The two fields that are NOT fixed-width — the committed leaf's identity and its content — are measured on their own axes: the identity below, the content in unboundedContentCarriage.
worstCase.payloadComposition: Each step's payload is the family's own bytes that ride that step's transaction: the spend redeemer, the thread datum the step consumes, and the thread datum it produces. step-04 produces no successor state, so its payload is the redeemer plus the datum it consumes. Reference inputs contribute an output reference each to the body and carry their datums in the referenced UTxOs rather than in this transaction, so step-02's two reference inputs do not enter the payload.

identifierWidthHeadroom.why: A `DepositId` is an `OutputReference`, and its CBOR width is not constant: the 32-byte transaction id is, but the output index is a Plutus integer, so a deposit created at a very high output index encodes wider than the sweep's worst-case key does. The axis is bounded and measured rather than ignored: taking an output index of 4294967295 — far above any transaction's real output count — widens the identity from 39 to 43 bytes and the binding step's payload from 1132 to 1140, because the identity rides step-01's payload exactly twice, in the membership key and in the handoff it produces. Eight bytes against a 15252-byte margin, so the identity-width axis cannot bind either.

valueSizeInvariance.why: The membership proof's size is measured to be independent of the leaf VALUE's size: rebuilding the 10000-leaf tree with a 4096-byte `l2_datum` on the challenged leaf changes the PHAS root, as it must, and leaves the proof at exactly 770 bytes. That is what separates the two axes below — the cardinality axis and the content-size axis are measured, not assumed, to be independent.

depthEnvelope.why: The cardinality axis is measured NOT to be the binding one. The step-01 payload minus its proof is 362 bytes, so the 16384-byte envelope admits 115 branch levels — one more overruns it — while the normative `max_deposit_count_v1` of 10000 realizes 6. Forcing d levels means grinding d nibbles of collision in the MPF's hashed key space, about 2^(4d) work, so exhausting the byte envelope by depth costs on the order of 2^460 work. The bound that binds this family is therefore the content-size axis below, not the depth of the tree.

unboundedContentCarriage.why: This is the axis the family's own doc comments describe, measured. The THREAD STATE never carries the unbounded content: step-02's and step-03's handoffs carry a 32-byte `committed_deposit_info_hash` and a 32-byte `event_datum_hash`, and step-04's carries two 32-byte commitments, so every handoff is a fixed size and the block producer cannot choose how many bytes each later step of the dispute pays for. The unbounded content rides a step transaction exactly twice, once each and never re-carried: step-01's redeemer must restate the committed `DepositInfo` because those are the very bytes the counted-root membership check hashes, and step-03's redeemer must open the authentic event datum because that is the preimage of the commitment step-02 retained. Both are single-step, disjoint transactions. The measured consequence is the ceiling above: the binding step is step-01, where a committed leaf whose `l2_datum` exceeds 14786 bytes leaves no room for the witness — and `ledger-state.ak` places no normative bound on that field, which is recorded as a residual finding rather than absorbed into this cell.

executionEnvelope.whyNotMeasured: Execution units at the adversarial depth cannot be measured in this tree: onchain/aiken/plutus.json is frozen and carries none of the family's eight titles, so the four step scripts have no `compiledCode` to evaluate, and the only lawful way to add a deeper on-chain measurement would be a new Aiken selector, which would break this row's exact 16-selector census. What IS measured is the peak of the 16 real handler runs under the pinned compiler, at the fixtures' own depth. The adversarial execution axis is carried as a residual finding owned by #617 rather than published as a margin.

output5AdversarialProofFit.whyLocalPass: The proof-fit question output 5 asks — does a step transaction of this family fit L1 at the worst case the protocol admits — is answered by measurement on the axis that binds: at `max_deposit_count_v1` leaves with the largest membership proof that cardinality admits, the binding step's payload is 1132 of 16384 bytes and every step clears the rule with margin. The two axes are measured independently rather than assumed independent, the cardinality axis is shown not to bind, and the content-size ceiling and the unmeasured execution axis are each owned by a named residual finding instead of being folded into this cell.

output6CatalogueAndDeployedIdentity.whyOpen: Nothing about the family's DEPLOYED identity is measurable at HEAD, and that is deliberate. The append-only catalogue order does not carry `fabricatedDeposit`, so there is no registered category to prove membership of; and the frozen blueprint carries 398 validators and none of this family's 8 titles, so the four step scripts have no `compiledCode`, no applied script hash and no reference-script identity to record. Both are owner-gated: blueprint regeneration and catalogue registration ride the #617 wave under ruling R5 (#510). The status is DERIVED from those two measurements — the count of the family's titles present in the blueprint, and the family's membership in the order constant — so #617 closes this cell without an edit here. The control title is required to be present in the same blueprint read, so "the family is missing" can never be satisfied by a failed or empty blueprint.

output7DaFirstEvidenceBuilder.retainedMaterialRoute: prepareFabricatedDepositFromRetainedDaV1 reconstructs the challenged block's committed deposit source set from the retained DA payload and then routes through prepareFabricatedDepositFromCommittedLeavesV1, so the proof is built from published, authenticated material rather than from operator-private state.

All seven cited titles are required to have EXECUTED and PASSED in the runner report, inside the family suite this gate spawns, rather than to exist in source.

output9EmulatorLifecycle.derivationNote: The shared `deriveVitestOutcome` helper refuses a skipped test outright — that is the ERR_FOCUSED_CHECK_NOT_EXECUTED discipline, and it is right for every suite that claims passage. This suite claims a boundary instead, so output 9 uses a purpose-built derivation: exactly one collected test, its assertion status exactly `skipped`, zero failed, exit 0, all four structural markers required inside the block's own body, and the eight-title absence the block itself asserts required to be the measured state of the blueprint. A block that silently started passing, or that collected two tests, or that skipped for a different reason, fails this cell.
output9EmulatorLifecycle.whyOpen: The on-chain half of the lifecycle — init, each of the four steps, the permanent fraud-proof token, removal — is not measurable in this tree, for exactly the reason the suite states at its boundary: the frozen blueprint has no `compiledCode` for the family's four step scripts. Everything short of evaluation IS measured, and the suite is required to stop deliberately rather than to be absent. The status is derived from the measured skip, so the #617 regeneration wave closes this cell without an edit here.

outputStatus.title: Normative rule statement and its violation identifier(s)
outputStatus.evidence: The rule is stated in full, in both of its arms and with the inclusion window that makes the fault a fault. Its identifier `fabricated-deposit` is measured in two declarations, and the deployed identifier is DERIVED rather than read: the append-only catalogue order is parsed, measured at 11 entries, measured NOT to contain `fabricatedDeposit`, and index 11 is encoded big-endian over the 4-byte width the catalogue declares to give `0000000b` — which both the on-chain constant and the SDK constant are then required to equal. Enforcement is on-chain rather than in a `RejectCodes` table, because this is a block-level fabrication rather than an L2 transaction rule, and the two decision sites that admit and convict are named and measured. The identifier is a RESERVED append slot, not a registered category; that pendency is output 6's and is owned by a residual finding.

outputStatus.title: Canonical evidence schema plus strict codec agreement across the boundary
outputStatus.evidence: Field-for-field, order-for-order parity is parsed out of each source and compared across the boundary for all seven records the family defines — three step `Args` plus the step-01 `Args` that carries the membership witness, and the three inter-step `State` handoffs — 30 fields in total, with the published list required to be the one both sides declare. Passage: 8/8 SDK byte-twin tests, which pin the leaf key, the leaf value, the event nonce, the event datum, the counted roots and all three handoffs against Aiken-measured absolutes, and 16/16 family tests.
